questions.question: Describe how coal is used to make steam in a power station.
questions.expected_answer: Coal from a nearby mine is carried on conveyor belts, crushed and ground into a fine powder, and blown into a furnace inside the boiler, where it burns at a very high temperature. The heat boils water in steel pipes around the furnace, turning it into steam at very high pressure.

questions.question: Explain how the turbine and generator produce electricity, and list the energy changes.
questions.expected_answer: The high-pressure steam rushes through the turbine and pushes on its curved blades, making the shaft spin very fast. The turbine shaft turns a generator, where a powerful magnet spins inside coils of copper wire, which makes electricity flow in the wire. The energy changes are chemical energy in coal, to heat energy in steam, to movement energy in the turbine, to electrical energy from the generator.

questions.question: How does electricity get from the power station to our homes?
questions.expected_answer: A transformer at the power station raises the voltage, and transmission lines on tall pylons carry the electricity across the country as part of the national grid. At substations near towns, transformers lower the voltage, and smaller lines or underground cables carry it along streets. A final transformer lowers it to about 230 volts, and it passes through the meter into the house wiring. The electricity travels in a giant circuit.
